100 ST assignment lines identical to realscale_st_n00100, PLUS 100 leading whole-line // comments of 16 characters, interleaved through the code the way real ST writes them. Same 100 ST assignment lines, 400 leading // comment lines instead of 100 -- the 4x point that turns the comment cost from a single delta into a slope, and brackets the real corpus ratio (6,925 comment lines against 24,017 total).

The same 100 ST assignment lines with a TRAILING // comment appended to each one -- same comment text as st_cmt_lead100_short but zero added lines. The same 100 ST assignment lines padded with 400 genuinely EMPTY source lines and no comments at all. 1000 ST assignments transcribing instr_cpt_n01000's CPT expression operand for operand: R := (D+D) * R - R/2 + 1.5. An ST assignment with an arithmetic right-hand side IS structurally a CPT expression, and this project already has a tier-aware CPT model (including the REAL-destination float model wired 2026-09-04, exact on 29/29 real rows). If this file lands on instr_cpt_n01000's 474,944, that whole model can be reused for ST assignments as-is instead of fitting a second one from scratch. 1000 single-operator ST assignments with a REAL destination and two DINT operands. Brackets st_expr_cpt_mirror_n01000 from below: the CPT model charges a first_operator term, per-operator extras, and an int->float conversion per non-float operand, so a 1-operator/2-int-operand case is the cleanest possible test of whether those same terms apply to ST.

1000 two-operator ST assignments with a DINT (integer) destination and no float anywhere. The CPT model prices integer and REAL destinations by completely different rules -- in float, operator TIER differences vanish and every non-float operand carries a conversion charge, neither of which applies to an all-integer expression. Read against st_expr_ops1_n01000 (REAL destination, same operand count), this says whether that destination-type split is real in ST too.

An ST routine used as a real JSR target with parameter passing -- SBR(5 inputs) at the top, 100 assignment statements, RET(1 output) at the bottom, called 100 times. This is a real shape, not a curiosity: the corpus carries 44 SBR and 42 RET calls inside ST routines. Everything this project knows about JSR parameter cost (B(n)=4+20n per call site, A(n)=104+20n per distinct target, output_param_cost=20) was fitted entirely on RLL targets; this is the only file that says whether an ST target is charged the same way. One XIC condition and 1 OTE outputs in series, each to its own bit, 1000 identical rungs. 8 XIC conditions and one OTE, 500 identical rungs, arranged as 1 parallel leg(s) of 8. Group A of the rung-shape sweep, and the core measurement of OQ-RUNGSHAPE: the instruction multiset and every operand are byte-identical across all four files, so the ONLY thing that moves is arrangement, and differencing consecutive files cancels the instructions and leaves the arrangement term alone. The logic weights were fitted on a corpus that is 9.4% branched against 68.7% in the sixteen real programs, which is the largest measured evidence gap in the project. A constant per-instruction error is already ruled out (CV 1.74) and branch FRACTION is ruled out as the carrier (r = -0.250); what correlates at r = -0.732 is the fraction of instructions INSIDE branches, which is exactly what these four files sweep. A fixed total of 4000 OTE instructions over 4000 distinct bits, packed 1 to a rung -- 4000 rungs. Group B of the rung-shape sweep. The instruction inventory and the tag inventory are identical in all five files, so rung COUNT is the only thing that moves and the per-rung term separates from the per-instruction term. OTE is the instrument because its isolated weight is confirmed exact at five counts from 10 to 5,000 and it takes one operand. OQ-RUNGSHAPE.

The same 400 controller tags -- 100 each of BOOL, INT, DINT and LINT, with identical names in every file -- declared grouped by type, in an order deliberately NOT sorted by width (DINT, BOOL, LINT, INT) -- the shape every existing tag family in the corpus uses, and the control the other five difference against; a width-sorted grouping would have duplicated narrowfirst exactly. OQ-TAGORDER: whether declaration ORDER changes what a tag multiset costs has never been tested, confirmed by search rather than assumed; every tag family in over 3,000 captured rows groups by type. An order effect is invisible to every test already run, because it changes cost without changing any count -- a per-tag rate, a per-type rate and a category scale all read identically across these six. The one existing order result says order is free INSIDE an AOI definition (the five aoidshape_order files all read -12), which is a different scope: a definition is a packed structure whose layout Logix controls, while a controller tag list is a series of independently allocated slots, and adjacent-tag alignment padding can only exist in the second. BOOL, INT, DINT and LINT are the four widths where padding could bite, and BOOL and DINT alone are 58% of the 31,532 tags in the sixteen real programs.

1000 MOV rungs into a SINT destination, source operand = the SINT tag LitSrc. Arm A of the literal-operand sweep, pair sint, and the measurement OQ-LITERALOPERAND turns on: (literal file - tag file) / 1000 is the per-slot cost of an immediate SINT literal, directly, with nothing fitted. The bench measured +4.000 for a REAL literal in a REAL-typed motion parameter; that case is 930 of the 52,195 unpriced literal slots in the seventeen real programs and the other 51,265 are integers at an unmeasured rate, which is why this arm exists. Hypothesis: an immediate costs the width of its type inline -- SINT 1, INT 2, DINT 4, LINT 8, REAL 4. LitSrc is DECLARED AND REFERENCED in BOTH files, by a byte-identical EQU, so this measures the operand and not a deleted tag. OQ-LITERALOPERAND.
